title: Veena (South Indian lute)
summary: The veena is the great plucked lute of South Indian classical music. A wide neck carries twenty-four fixed frets over a big carved wooden bowl, a small gourd rests near the head, and four playing strings are joined by side strings that keep the beat. Players pull a string sideways on its fret to bend and shake a note.
howToPlay: Four strings run down the wide neck, the lowest on the left. Each lane sits at the fret where that note is played.
A bead slides down the string toward its fret. Pluck the lane just as the bead lands.
Try the slow rising phrase first, then the eight-beat cycle, then the running phrase.
Notes ring long, so the slow phrases leave room to listen.
rules: The seven steps used are a bright scale with a raised fourth, from the lower seventh up to the high third.
The eight-beat cycle is counted in four groups of two.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The veena has been played in South India for centuries. Makers still carve the bowl and neck by hand from jackfruit wood, and players learn phrase by phrase by listening to a teacher and repeating.
credits: Tradition: the South Indian veena; phrases written for this game
